title: Chokeberry-exercise-study
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the combined effects of regular physical activity and the consumption of an extract/concentrate from aronia berries, which could offer particular benefits for people with prediabetic metabolism. Previous studies have demonstrated anti-inflammatory/antioxidant and, in some cases, anabolic effects of consuming aronia juice or extract. Combining this with exercise, particularly strength training, is promising and represents an
innovative approach to the treatment of prediabetes, which could contribute to successful remission in some people with this pre-existing condition.

interventions.name: 8-week strength training (twice a week) + daily placebo
8-week strength training (twice a week) + daily supplementation of chokeberry extract (in the morning and evening)
8-week strength training (twice a week) + daily supplementation of chokeberry concentrate (in the morning and evening)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
HbA1c 5.7-6.4%, fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dl
Exclusion criteria:
Chronic diseases except for factors of metabolic syndrome (obesity, hyperlipidemia, high blood pressure, and any corresponding medication). Diseases leading to exclusion include, in particular, various types of diseases that limit performance or training (severe cardiovascular diseases, e.g., uncontrollable cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure (EF<55), peripheral arterial disease (Fontaine stage ≥ II), degenerative joint diseases, or muscular diseases). Other exclusion criteria include: hormone therapy (except L-thyroxine), smoking status, acute oncological diseases or a history thereof (< 5 years), infections (HIV, hepatitis), psychiatric disorders, and/or addiction.
